_meta.title: Recommendation pilot — everyday AI assistants
_meta.purpose: One category, six alternatives, eight criteria. Feeds the preview at /recommend. Not a general scoring layer and no aggregate score.
_meta.provenance_note: A model read each source; no human re-read them. Nothing is marked human-reviewed.

identity_model.why: Three different things get confused when a product is described by one 'provider'. They answer different questions and must be applied only to the question they can answer.
identity_model.product_provider: Who operates the consumer product. Governance criteria attach here.
identity_model.model_provider: Whose model serves it. May differ from the product provider, and may vary by surface.
identity_model.model_release: Which specific model version. Licensing criteria attach here.
identity_model.rule: Unknown model routing does NOT invalidate an established product-provider identity, nor any provider-level governance finding. It only leaves model-level questions unanswered.

status_separation.retrieval_status: Whether we could fetch the source. 'blocked' means a server refused an automated request — it is not evidence about the product.
status_separation.factual_status: Whether the fact is established, and from what kind of source.
status_separation.rule: A retrieval failure is recorded separately from factual uncertainty and never presented as doubt about the product.

claim_types.established_outcome: Recorded in a filing, licence, index, court record or official product documentation.
claim_types.company_statement: The company's own description of itself.
claim_types.allegation: Claimed by a party to a dispute, not settled.

status_values.proposed: Reported or announced, not established as in force.

decision_rules.soft_by_default: A preference explains and orders. It never excludes, and an unknown preference neither rewards nor penalises.
decision_rules.hard_opt_in: A criterion excludes only when the user explicitly designates it a requirement, and only where the evidence can decide.
decision_rules.unknown_requirement: An unknown hard requirement is never shown as satisfied. The option goes to a separate 'requirement not confirmed' group — visible, not shortlisted, not excluded.
decision_rules.no_filling: Shortlist slots are never filled to reach a number.

corrections_applied: Anthropic’s statement that exported data cannot be imported into another personal Claude account is account-to-account evidence. It no longer drives cross-service migration, which is a different question with a different destination.
Cross-service migration is unconfirmed for all six until evidence addresses the destination product and what must transfer.
A requirement is never downgraded to a preference because evidence is missing. It stays a requirement and returns an explicit unconfirmed state.
Criterion labels are written to be understood on their own; the scope caveats sit in an evidence section rather than in front of the label.

category.label: Everyday AI assistants
category.definition: A general-purpose conversational assistant used for drafting, summarising, explaining and answering questions.

why_this_category.user_relevance: The highest-frequency personal AI choice most people make, and genuinely substitutable.
why_this_category.evidence_coverage: Six providers are already makers in this dataset, and official help centres document the product behaviour users care about.
why_this_category.honest_caveat: Capability differences are real and not assessed here.

functional_requirements.label: Usable in a browser without a developer account

criteria.label: No single person holds more than half the votes
criteria.concept: Whether any single person holds more than 50% of the votes.
criteria.does_not_establish: That no individual controls the company, or that no one can override the board. Control can also run through board seats, class rights, supermajority provisions or contract. We only report the voting-power figure.
criteria.distinct_from: Founder-bloc voting power. Two founders with 52.7% between them is not one founder with 52.7%.
criteria.plain: Whether one person could outvote everyone else.

criteria.label: The founders together hold less than half the votes
criteria.concept: Whether founders acting together hold more than 50% of the votes.
criteria.does_not_establish: That the founders act together in practice, or that they control the company by other means. A bloc requires its members to agree.
criteria.plain: Whether the founders, voting as a group, could outvote everyone else.

criteria.label: Who can appoint and remove the board
criteria.concept: Which party can elect or remove directors, separately from economic ownership.
criteria.plain: Which party picks the directors, separately from who owns the shares.

criteria.label: A legal duty to weigh more than shareholder returns
criteria.concept: A legal structure currently obliging the company to weigh non-shareholder interests.
criteria.does_not_establish: That the obligation has changed any decision.
criteria.distinct_from: Commitment continuity — whether earlier commitments were kept.
criteria.plain: A company structure that currently obliges directors to consider people other than shareholders.

criteria.label: Past public-benefit promises have been kept
criteria.concept: Whether public-benefit mechanisms this provider adopted have been kept or withdrawn.
criteria.does_not_establish: What the provider will do next.
criteria.plain: Whether commitments of this kind, once adopted, were later withdrawn.

criteria.label: You can download your own conversations
criteria.concept: Whether you can download your conversations and account data from the product.
criteria.does_not_establish: That the export can be used anywhere else.
criteria.distinct_from: Migrating to another service, which needs somewhere to import it.
criteria.plain: A way to get your chat history and account data out of the product.

criteria.label: You can move your content to another account with the same provider
criteria.plain: Transferring your history from one account to another at the same company.
criteria.concept: Whether exported content can be loaded into a different account at the same provider.
criteria.does_not_establish: Anything about moving to a different company’s product. A provider can refuse account-to-account transfer and still place no obstacle in front of taking your data elsewhere.
criteria.distinct_from: Cross-service migration, which is about a different destination entirely.

criteria.label: You can move your content to a different company’s product
criteria.concept: Whether exported content can be imported into a competing product and used there.
criteria.does_not_establish: Anything about model portability, and nothing about transfers within the same provider.
criteria.distinct_from: Account-to-account transfer at the same provider, which has a different destination and different evidence.
criteria.plain: Taking your history out of one product and using it in a competitor’s.
criteria.requires_evidence_about: Both the destination product and what actually has to transfer for the move to be useful.

criteria.label: You could run the model yourself
criteria.concept: Whether the specific model serving the product is published under a licence letting you run it yourself.
criteria.does_not_establish: That the hosted assistant is portable, or that your content comes with you.
criteria.distinct_from: Export and migration, which are about your data, not the model.
criteria.plain: Whether the model serving this product is published under a licence letting you host it.

assessments.claim: ChatGPT offers a self-serve export: Settings → Data controls → Export data. A download link arrives by email or SMS, can take up to 7 days, and expires 24 hours after it arrives.
assessments.source: OpenAI Help Center, article 7260999 'How do I export my ChatGPT history and data?'
assessments.scope: Consumer accounts. Business, Enterprise and Healthcare workspaces have no self-serve export.
assessments.uncertainty: help.openai.com refused automated fetching (403), so the article was read through search indexing rather than directly. The article is official; the block is on our side.

assessments.claim: Claude offers a self-serve export: Settings → Privacy → Export data, available on Free, Pro and Max plans. The export contains conversation data and account data, and arrives as an emailed download link valid 24 hours.
assessments.source: support.claude.com article 9450526 'Export your Claude data', fetched directly
assessments.scope: Individual accounts. Team and Enterprise members have no self-serve option; their Primary Owner exports instead.
assessments.uncertainty: Low. Read from the official help article.

assessments.claim: Gemini Apps data can be exported through Google Takeout. The archive contains JSON files with prompts, responses, timestamps and conversation identifiers.
assessments.source: Google Gemini Apps Help, 'Download your Gemini Apps data' (article 16920332)
assessments.scope: There is no in-app export. Note a trap: the 'Gemini' entry in Takeout exports Gems (custom personas), not conversations — conversation history sits under 'Gemini Apps'.
assessments.uncertainty: The official help article was read through search indexing; gemini.google.com itself could not be fetched.

assessments.claim: Consumer Copilot activity history can be exported from the Microsoft privacy dashboard, which downloads a CSV file. A structured data request is also available through the Microsoft Privacy Request Center.
assessments.source: Microsoft Support, 'Manage your Copilot activity history in the privacy dashboard'
assessments.scope: Consumer Copilot activity history, retained up to 18 months by default. CSV is a thinner format than the JSON others provide.
assessments.uncertainty: Read through search indexing of the official support pages rather than fetched directly.

assessments.claim: Vibe provides an in-product export control: 'Simply click on the Export button to download all your Vibe data.'
assessments.source: help.mistral.ai article 347623 'How do I export my data from Vibe?', fetched directly
assessments.uncertainty: Low for the mechanism's existence. Some secondary sources claimed no native export existed; the official help article contradicts them, and the official article is preferred.

assessments.claim: No self-serve export control is documented. Secondary sources report that export is available by emailing service@deepseek.com, and third-party browser extensions exist.
assessments.source: Secondary guides; no official DeepSeek help-centre article located
assessments.uncertainty: This is an absence claim from secondary sources — we did not find an export control, which is not the same as establishing there is none. Recorded as unconfirmed rather than as a failure.

assessments.claim: Anthropic states that exported data cannot be imported into another personal Claude account and that migrating data between personal accounts is not supported.
assessments.scope: Transfer between two personal Claude accounts, stated by the provider. It says nothing about moving content to a different company’s product.
assessments.uncertainty: Low as to what Anthropic states, and correctly scoped: this is an account-transfer finding. An earlier pass wrongly used it to exclude Claude from cross-service migration, which it does not address.

assessments.claim: Whether a Claude export can be imported into a different company’s product is not documented either way.
assessments.uncertainty: Anthropic’s statement about account-to-account transfer does not answer this. Establishing it needs evidence about the destination product and what would have to transfer. Counts neither way.

assessments.uncertainty: Export format is known for most of these, but no import path was researched. Counts neither way.

assessments.claim: No single Alphabet shareholder holds a majority of votes. Page holds 27.1% and Brin 25.2% of total voting power individually.
assessments.source: Alphabet 2026 annual meeting proxy statement, via reporting of the filing
assessments.scope: Voting power at Alphabet Inc., the parent. It does not establish that no individual controls Alphabet by other means, and it says nothing about DeepMind's internal governance.
assessments.uncertainty: Percentages read from reporting of the proxy, not the filing itself. Internally consistent with the reported 52.7% combined.

assessments.claim: Page and Brin together hold 52.7% of Alphabet's total voting power, through Class B shares carrying ten votes each. Class C carries none.
assessments.source: Alphabet 2026 annual meeting proxy statement, via reporting of the filing
assessments.scope: Combined voting power only. It does not establish that they vote together, nor that either can act alone.
assessments.uncertainty: As above.

assessments.claim: Microsoft has a single class of common stock with one vote per share and no supervoting class. The largest holder in the 2025 proxy is Vanguard at 8.95%.
assessments.source: Microsoft DEF 14A proxy statement filed 2025-12-05, via reporting of the filing
assessments.scope: Voting power only. It does not establish that no individual influences Microsoft by other means.
assessments.uncertainty: Read through search of the filing rather than from the document itself. Ownership percentages move; the share-class structure does not.

assessments.claim: Microsoft has no dual-class structure giving founders outsized control, and no founder bloc appears among its principal shareholders.
assessments.source: Microsoft DEF 14A proxy statement filed 2025-12-05, via reporting of the filing
assessments.scope: Share-class structure and principal shareholders as disclosed.
assessments.uncertainty: As above.
